clue.text: Outsiders in the jazz quartet

indicators.note: the outsiders of a word are the letters standing at its two edges, first and last

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz, the New Orleans style revived in Britain

explanation.surface: Some misfits who play in a four-piece jazz band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outsiders in' takes the first and last letters of 'the'; trad is the British name for traditional jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a group or set of four things.

clue.text: How to send messages, in a moment, on the course

parts.note: a tick is British informal for a moment, as in 'just a tick'
a tack is a course of action, or a ship's course

explanation.surface: Getting word out quickly while at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: It is the arm-waving sign language British racecourse bookmakers used to signal odds, so 'on the course' also colours the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a signalling system of hand gestures used by bookmakers to pass odds to one another.

clue.text: Baggage gets to writer out East

indicators.note: says the letter for East is left out of the writer's name

parts.note: Anthony Trollope was a Victorian novelist

explanation.surface: Luggage is forwarded to an author living abroad in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops the E from the Victorian novelist's name. 'Baggage' is not luggage but an old insult for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned derogatory words for a disreputable or saucy woman.

clue.text: Roasting very long fish

parts.note: assai is the Italian musical direction meaning very, as in allegro assai
the ling is a long slender fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Cooking an extremely lengthy fish in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roasting' is not cooking but criticising fiercely; 'very' is the musical direction seen in allegro assai.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in the sense of attacking someone with harsh criticism.

clue.text: Help one gets, for a start, in front of better

definitions.text: Help one gets, for a start, in front of better

indicators.note: says the first two pieces stand ahead of the piece that follows

parts.note: to give a hand is to give help
the Roman numeral for one is I
to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: A weaker player is given a head start over a stronger one.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: 'in front of' places the first two pieces before the word for 'better' as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf or racing it is the allowance, often a head start, given to the weaker competitor against a superior one.

clue.text: One whose work is self-explanatory?

parts.note: read literally: a writer whose book explains the writer's own self, by telling their life story

explanation.definitionFit: Such a writer sets out the story of their own life, so the book literally accounts for its creator.

clue.text: Name a god that's strangely composed

definitions.text: Name a god that's strangely composed

indicators.note: put together in an odd way, so the letters are assembled in an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: A request to identify a deity with an oddly calm manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is definition and wordplay: 'strangely composed' rearranges N, A and GOD. The Philistine deity was pictured as half man, half fish.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the Philistine deity of the Bible, traditionally shown as part man and part fish, an odd make-up.

clue.text: Shell that is doing for a non-combatant

parts.note: a conch is a large spiral sea shell
ie abbreviates the Latin id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: An artillery round that kills someone who was not even fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell' is a sea shell, not artillery. The answer is British slang for a conscientious objector, one who refuses to fight on principle.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a conscientious objector, who refuses on principle to bear arms.

clue.text: Times at the top in 1979 and 1987, for example

definitions.meaning: periods when someone is at their best, the peak years of a life
both numbers can be divided only by themselves and one

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the best periods of a life and numbers with no divisors but themselves and one.

clue.text: As trapeze artist may need to be, unlike thief

definitions.text: As trapeze artist may need to be, unlike thief

parts.words: As trapeze artist may need to be, unlike thief
parts.note: a flyer must be grabbed by a colleague during the circus turn, while a burglar hopes never to be seized while doing the deed

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being discovered red-handed also literally describes a flyer being grabbed mid-performance.

clue.text: Food from the interior of France — it's so flaky

indicators.note: something flaky falls to pieces, so the letters come apart and are rearranged
the interior of a word is what is left inside once its first and last letters go

explanation.surface: A French pastry from the heart of the country, crumbling at a touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the interior of' strips France to RANC, and 'flaky' rearranges RANC with ITSSO. The whole clue also describes the pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a crescent-shaped French breakfast pastry is something to eat.

clue.text: Spirits in the very first verse?

parts.note: the Bible's opening verse is in Genesis, abbreviated Gen
chapter one, verse one, written in Roman numerals as I and I

explanation.surface: Ghosts or strong drink turning up in a poem's opening lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible's opening verse is Genesis chapter 1 verse 1, written as an abbreviation followed by two Roman ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A plural of genius in its sense of guardian or attendant supernatural beings.

clue.text: Powerful relation

definitions.meaning: a blow or argument that has a marked effect
the act of relating or narrating a story

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means effective or striking, and as a noun it is the narrating of a tale.

clue.text: Something followed by death female appearing near end

definitions.text: Something followed by death female appearing near end

indicators.note: says the female word is placed inside the other, close to its last letter

parts.note: bane is an old word for death or destruction
she is the pronoun for a female

explanation.surface: An ominous woman who turns up just before somebody dies.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: 'appearing near end' puts the female pronoun inside the word for death, just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore she is a wailing woman spirit whose cry warns that someone in the house is about to die.

clue.text: Head of French state in Italian resort

parts.note: cap is the French word for a head or headland, as in Cap Ferrat
RI is the abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island

explanation.surface: The French president taking a holiday on the Italian coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the French president; in fact the French word for a headland is followed by an American state's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a holiday island in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Beats tiger heartlessly, and other wild cats

indicators.note: without its heart, so the word loses the letters in its middle

parts.note: ounces are snow leopards, wild cats of central Asia

explanation.surface: Someone cruelly thrashes a tiger and various other big cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes IGE, the middle of 'tiger', leaving TR. An ounce is another name for the snow leopard.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: defeats heavily or thrashes.

clue.text: Stupidly take it with ten, if without king — or queen

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so the jumbled letters go round the royal piece
to take the words stupidly is to handle them in a muddled, disordered way

parts.note: ER is the royal cipher of a King Edward, Edwardus Rex

explanation.surface: A card player foolishly wins a trick with the ten when holding no court cards.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a card game, but 'Stupidly take' makes NEFTITI from the three short words, and 'without' has its old sense of outside. A King Edward signed himself Edwardus Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: she was the royal wife of the Egyptian pharaoh Akhenaten.

clue.text: Keen to have stringed instruments in band

indicators.note: says the instruments are placed inside the word for band

parts.note: a set is a band or group of people
harps are instruments with strings

explanation.surface: An eager musician wants violins and cellos in the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the instruments inside a word for a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an old word for hungry or eager.

clue.text: Ringmaster introduces turn man driving horses?

indicators.note: the composer's name brings the other word inside itself

parts.note: Wagner composed the Ring cycle of operas, so he is whimsically the master of the Ring
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: The circus ringmaster announces an act featuring a man with a team of horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringmaster' is not a circus figure but the composer of the Ring cycle; 'introduces' has his name take the word for a turn inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: He is someone who drives a horse-drawn cart, in the older double-G spelling.

clue.text: A learner taken in by, say, imperial French scholar

indicators.note: says the letter for learner is swallowed by the word that follows

parts.note: an imperial is one example of a beard, a small pointed tuft under the lip
L is the plate shown by a learner driver in Britain

explanation.surface: A student is fooled by an academic from the days of the French empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' puts L, the British learner driver's plate, inside a word that an imperial (a small pointed tuft under the lip) exemplifies.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Peter of this name was a twelfth-century Parisian philosopher, famous for his love of Heloise.

clue.text: Interval, for players making a score of 100, for example

definitions.meaning: to musicians it is the interval spanning five notes of the scale

definitions.text: making a score of 100, for example
definitions.meaning: a score is twenty, which is this fraction of a hundred

explanation.definitionFit: It is a musical interval, and also the fraction that turns a hundred into twenty.

clue.text: Bird's two followers

definitions.note: the possessive is read as 'bird is', so the answer is simply a bird

parts.note: a fan is a follower or devotee
a tail is someone who follows and watches a suspect

explanation.surface: A bird has a couple of admirers trailing after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a kind of pigeon, and also a small flycatcher of Australasia.

clue.text: He and I joining university, in position of control

indicators.note: says the two single letters are placed inside the word for the position of control

parts.note: the helm is where a ship is steered, so figuratively the position of command

explanation.surface: Two men start at the same college, each holding a post of authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is not a pronoun but a chemical symbol; 'in' puts I and U inside the steering position.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the chemical symbol for this light gas.

clue.text: English trees rot!

parts.note: the yew is one tree
the ash is another tree

explanation.surface: A lament that the nation's woodland is decaying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trees' supplies two different trees one after the other; 'rot' is not decay but an exclamation meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British exclamations meaning nonsense or humbug.

clue.text: Wine essential for seasonal oysters removed from bed

parts.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
oysters are traditionally eaten only when there is an R in the month

explanation.surface: A bottle that must accompany shellfish freshly taken from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The old rule is that oysters are in season only in months spelt with an R. 'bed' is where one sleeps, not an oyster bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym for being up and about after sleeping.

clue.text: Capture back with rook — that's mate

indicators.note: says the word for capture is to be read from its last letter to its first

parts.note: to entrap is to capture or snare
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A chess player retakes with the rook and delivers checkmate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ENTRAP into PARTNE, and R is chess notation for rook. 'mate' is a companion, not checkmate.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a spouse or companion.

clue.text: Unsuitable for paint work

indicators.note: to work material is to knead or shape it, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is not fit to do a decorating job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' looks like a noun paired with paint, but it tells you to rearrange the letters of 'paint'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: not fitting or appropriate.

clue.text: Mixture of races in a melting-pot, originally

definitions.text: Mixture of races in a melting-pot, originally

indicators.note: a mixture is a blend, so the letters that follow are blended into a new order
the origin of a word is the letter it starts with

explanation.surface: A nation formed from many peoples blended together in one great pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is definition and wordplay at once: 'Mixture of' rearranges RACES, IN, A and M, the letter 'originally' takes from melting-pot.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is famously called a melting-pot, its people descended from immigrants of many nations.

clue.text: 60's youth getting inspiration for love lyrics? Not so fast!

parts.note: a mod was a member of a British 1960s youth group known for sharp suits and scooters
Erato is the Greek muse of love poetry

explanation.surface: A sixties teenager looking for ideas for a love song is told to slow down.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods were a British 1960s youth subculture of sharp suits and scooters; the muse of love poetry follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction telling players to take a restrained, medium pace.

clue.text: Girl in Rome would put sex before love, to be permissive

indicators.note: says the Roman piece comes ahead of the piece for love

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, which a Roman would write as the numeral VI
love is a score of nothing in tennis, written O
to let is to allow or permit

explanation.surface: A liberated young woman in Italy ranks physical passion above romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex' is the Latin word for six, which a Roman writes as a numeral; 'before' places it ahead of the tennis zero.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a female first name.
